title: Talent tracker: WPP, BBDO, Meta, HDFC and Google Cloud among this week’s key leadership moves
excerpt: New Delhi: The past week brought a number of leadership changes across the industry, with senior executives stepping into new roles, taking on broader responsibilities and moving to new organisations. The developments covered marketing, communications, strategy, product, sales, media and business functions. Jon Cook to leave WPP; Eric Campbell to take over as VML global CEO Jon Cook, Global CEO of VML and CEO of WPP Creative, will leave WPP after three decades. He will stay in both roles until March 2027. Eric Campbell, CEO of VML and WPP Creative in North America, will take over as Global CEO of VML in March 2027. He has been with VML for more than 25 years. McCann CEO Tyler Turnbull set to take over as WPP Creative Global CEO WPP is set to appoint Tyler Turnbull, currently Global CEO of McCann, as Global CEO of WPP Creative. He will succeed Jon Cook, who is scheduled to leave the company in March 2027. Turnbull has led McCann since December 2025 and was earlier Global CEO of FCB. WPP Creative brings together agencies including Ogilvy, VML, Grey, AKQA, Burson, Landor and Design Bridge & Partners. Josy Paul named Chairman and Group Chief Creative Officer at BBDO Group India BBDO Group India has elevated Josy Paul to Chairman and Group Chief Creative Officer. He will oversee the creative vision across the group's three agencies: BBDO India, Ulka and Mudra. Paul co-founded BBDO India in 2008. His elevation follows Jitender Dabas's appointment as CEO of BBDO Group India in February. Stagwell launches new global media agency Stagwell Media; Alap Ghosh to lead India Stagwell has launched Stagwell Media, a new global media agency built on the foundation of Assembly. It will be led by Liz Rutgersson as CEO, with Alap Ghosh as CEO, India. The agency will operate across more than 50 markets with over 2,300 employees. Its clients include Lenovo, DP World, Mastercard and P&G. Former LinkedIn CEO Ryan Roslansky to leave Microsoft at year-end Ryan Roslansky, Executive Vice President at Microsoft and former CEO of LinkedIn, will leave Microsoft at the end of 2026. He will remain until then as an Advisor to Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella. Roslansky joined LinkedIn in May 2009 and was its CEO from 2020 to April 2026. Dan Shapero will continue as CEO of LinkedIn, reporting to Nadella. Former ICICI Bank Executive Director Anup Bagchi named HDFC Bank MD and CEO HDFC Bank has appointed Anup Bagchi as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer for three years, effective October 27, 2026. The Reserve Bank of India approved the appointment on October 1. Bagchi will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose tenure ends on October 26. He has been Managing Director and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance since June 2023. Ravi Garg takes on APAC enterprise business mandate at Meta Meta has named Ravi Garg Managing Director, Enterprise Business, APAC. He announced the move in a LinkedIn post. Garg was previously Country Director, Business Messaging and Payments at WhatsApp, a role he held from July 2021. Before that, he spent 13 years at Microsoft. Amit Kumar takes interim charge of Google Cloud India after Sreedharan moves to Sarvam AI Google Cloud has appointed Amit Kumar as Interim Head of its India business following Sashikumar Sreedharan's departure. Karan Bajwa, President, Asia Pacific, Google Cloud, confirmed the change in a LinkedIn post. Kumar joined Google Cloud in March 2021 and has been serving as Managing Director, Digital Native Business. Sreedharan had led Google Cloud India since July 2025. Hershey Company names Amanda Almond as President, International The Hershey Company has named Amanda Almond as President, International, effective October 12, 2026. She succeeds Rohit Grover, who has spent 27 years with Hershey. Almond was most recently Regional Managing Director for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at Vinarchy. She earlier spent 12 years at Bacardi. Puneet Sharma joins NielsenIQ as Managing Director for India NielsenIQ (NIQ) has appointed Puneet Sharma as Managing Director, India, effective September 30, 2026. He will lead the company's commercial strategy and business operations in the country. Sharma most recently served as Sales Director at Kenvue. He has more than 20 years of experience, including roles at Johnson & Johnson, The Coca-Cola Company and Bacardi. Cipla Health names Gaurav Kaul as MD and CEO Gaurav Kaul has taken charge as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Cipla Health. He announced the move in a LinkedIn post. Kaul joined Cipla in March 2021 and was most recently Chief Commercial Head Rx, India Business. He has also worked at GSK Consumer Healthcare India, Novartis Consumer Healthcare and Cadbury. Gbile Adewunmi to lead Cummins India alongside global Industrial Markets role Cummins India has appointed Gbile Adewunmi as Managing Director and India Regional Leader, effective November 1, 2026. He will retain his current role as Vice-President, Power Systems Industrial Markets at Cummins. Cummins India was established in 1962 and is headquartered in Pune. Hindware names Shashvat Somany Joint Managing Director to lead bathware and pipes Hindware Limited has appointed Shashvat Somany as Joint Managing Director. He will be responsible for its bathware and pipes businesses. Somany was previously Head of Strategy at Somany Impresa Group. He has also worked at AGI Greenpac and Deloitte Consulting. JioStar expands entertainment digital ad sales team with senior hires across branding, commerce and content IPs JioStar has added three senior leaders to its Entertainment Digital Ad Sales team. Sudhir Shukla joins as EVP (LCS Branding), Rachit Jain as SVP (LCS Commerce) and Junaid Khwaja as SVP (Content IPs). Shukla was most recently Chief Operating Officer at More Retail, Jain co-founded Sparkonomy, and Khwaja was National Sales Head at Dream11. The appointments were communicated internally by Bhaskar Ramesh, Head – Entertainment Sales, Digital. Rubika Liyaquat back at News18; to head Rajasthan channel, anchor 7 pm on News18 India Rubika Liyaquat has returned to Network18 as Managing Editor of News18 Rajasthan. She will also anchor the 7 pm slot on News18 India. Liyaquat left News18 India in May 2026 and joined Times Now Navbharat in June, exiting the channel in September. She will report to Jyoti Kamal, Managing Editor, News18 India. WPP Media appoints Seshadri Shankaran as Senior Vice President WPP Media has appointed Seshadri Shankaran as Senior Vice-President, Client Investments, Marketplace and Partnerships, India. He joined in September 2026. Shankaran was previously General Manager at Bennett Coleman & Co. He earlier spent a decade at GroupM, most recently as National Head, Agency Investments, and has also worked at Star TV and Times Internet. He has also worked at OMD India, Starcom MediaVest Group India and Madison Communications India. Ankitha Acharya takes up Global Strategy Director role for Nestlé at WPP Media Ankitha Acharya has joined WPP Media as Global Strategy Director, Nestlé. She announced the move in a LinkedIn post. Acharya was previously Brand Strategy Director for Emerging Markets, Adidas, at EssenceMediacom. She has also worked at Mindshare, Wavemaker and Performics India. Diageo India elevates Mohit Cherian to Vice President, Customer Marketing Diageo India has elevated Mohit Cherian to Vice President, Customer Marketing. title: Current Affairs One-Liner: 10th October 2026
excerpt: National On 8 October 2026, the Central Government approved a 30% trade-margin cap on non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines to make cancer treatment more affordable. The Department of Pharmaceuticals stated that the measure could reduce the prices of certain medicines by up to 70%, generating estimated annual savings of ₹2,500 crore for patients. An expert committee under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) will finalise the medicines covered, while the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) will issue the implementing notification. The decision extends price protection beyond scheduled medicines already subject to ceiling prices. On 9 October 2026, the Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved a proposal to rename Noida International Airport at Jewar as Narendra Modi International Airport. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced the decision following a Cabinet meeting. The airport is being developed in Gautam Buddha Nagar district to improve air connectivity across the National Capital Region and western Uttar Pradesh. The proposed name recognises Prime Minister Narendra Modi's association with the project. The Cabinet's approval is an important step in the naming process, although the relevant administrative formalities must also be completed. On 5 October 2026, the West Bengal Government approved the Bhagini Nivedita Scheme to provide ₹50,000 to unmarried women pursuing undergraduate education. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that eligible beneficiaries would receive ₹17,000 in their first year, ₹17,000 in their second year and ₹16,000 in their third year. The scheme is scheduled to begin in January 2027 and aims to reduce financial barriers to women's higher education. It will replace the Kanyashree 2 component, which provided a one-time grant of ₹25,000. On 8 October 2026, Gujarat's Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad received recognition through a Geographical Indication (GI) registration. The traditional sweet is associated with the Shree Arasuri Ambaji Mata Temple in Banaskantha district. The registration was obtained by the Shree Arasuri Ambaji Mata Devsthan Trust under Class 30, which covers confectionery and related food products. The certificate was issued on 1 October, with a formal presentation scheduled for 11 October 2026. GI protection helps preserve the product's geographical identity, traditional preparation and reputation against unauthorised commercial imitation. On 18 September 2026, the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) issued revised Standard Operating Procedures for updating names in Aadhaar. The guidelines clarify document requirements for minor spelling corrections, major name changes, errors in regional languages and changes following marriage, divorce or other recognised circumstances. A complete legal name change generally requires supporting evidence such as a Gazette notification. Under UIDAI's existing demographic update policy, an Aadhaar holder can ordinarily update their name twice, with an exception process available thereafter. The revised procedure aims to strengthen uniformity, accuracy and identity verification. On 10 October 2026, reports highlighted the recovery of the hard-ground Barasingha population in Madhya Pradesh's Satpura Tiger Reserve to 303 animals. The population has grown following a long-term reintroduction and conservation programme involving animals from Kanha Tiger Reserve. Conservation measures include grassland restoration, scientific habitat management, protection from threats and community participation. The Barasingha, also called the swamp deer, is an important species in India's grassland ecosystems. Authorities are considering wildlife corridors to improve habitat connectivity and maintain genetic diversity, supporting the population's long-term conservation. On 5 October 2026, a critically endangered Red-headed Vulture (Sarcogyps calvus) was sighted in the Munsiyari region of Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand. The bird was observed by members of the local conservation organisation Monal near Patalthod at an elevation of approximately 2,650 metres. The species is classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List and is recognisable by its bare red head and dark plumage. The observation is important for monitoring threatened scavenging birds in Himalayan ecosystems, where vultures play an essential role in removing animal carcasses. International: On 8 October 2026, the United States Department of Justice announced additional criminal charges against former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. A superseding indictment filed in the Southern District of New York accused the couple of conspiring to commit torture, alongside existing allegations involving narcoterrorism, cocaine trafficking and weapons offences. Prosecutors alleged that political opponents and American citizens were subjected to severe mistreatment under the former administration. The charges remain allegations, and both defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court. On 9 October 2026, a powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama, triggering tsunami warnings and widespread evacuations. According to the United States Geological Survey, the earthquake occurred at a depth of approximately 12.6 kilometres, around 200 kilometres from Panama City. A second major tremor and numerous aftershocks followed. The earthquake caused structural damage and electricity disruptions in several provinces, although the Panama Canal remained operational. Authorities subsequently lifted the initial tsunami warning. Panama lies in a seismically active region influenced by interactions among tectonic plates near the Pacific Ring of Fire. Economy: On 9 October 2026, the Spices Board India and ICAR–Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) discussed the development of the Bharat Spice Map at a national seminar in Kochi, Kerala. The initiative aims to identify the geographical distribution of spice crops, distinctive varieties and quality characteristics using geospatial technology and scientific research. It will help connect domestic spice production with industrial requirements, identify high-value export opportunities and reduce import dependence. The seminar formed part of the Reform Utsav initiative and was inaugurated by ICAR Secretary Gyanendra D. Tripathi. On 9 October 2026, the Union Government approved Telangana's proposal to seek ₹5,000 crore in external assistance from Germany's development bank KfW. The proposed funding is part of the Telangana Climate Resilient Urban Transformation Initiative (Telangana-CRUTI), a programme valued at approximately ₹7,143 crore. It seeks to improve urban sewerage, wastewater treatment, drinking-water supply and stormwater management. The Greater Warangal Comprehensive Sewerage and Wastewater Management Transformation Project is a major component. The Central Government's approval concerns the external funding proposal; it should not be treated as confirmation that the entire loan has already been disbursed. On 4 August 2026, the World Bank released its World Development Report 2026, titled The Promise of Artificial Intelligence. The report examines how artificial intelligence can support economic growth, productivity, employment and public-service delivery in developing countries. It estimates that 4.5% of existing jobs in low- and middle-income countries face automation risks, compared with 14.2% in high-income countries. It also identifies opportunities for productivity improvements in developing economies. The report recommends an Adopt, Adapt and Advance framework, emphasising digital infrastructure, local-language data, electricity, skills and institutional capacity. Sports: On 9 October 2026, Delhi golfer Keya Kumar Badugu won the women's title at the IGU Bio-Gen Rotary Southern India Golf Championship for Ladies and Junior Girls. The competition was held at the Karnataka Golf Association course in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Badugu defeated Kolkata's Anaahat Bindra in a playoff after both golfers completed the 54-hole competition with identical scores of one-under-par 215. Badugu recorded rounds of 73, 71 and 71, while Bindra scored 70, 72 and 73. Priya Kumari finished third with an aggregate score of 220. On 9 October 2026, South African swimmer Pieter Coetze established a new world record in the men's 50-metre backstroke (short-course) event at the World Aquatics Swimming World Cup in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. He completed the event in 22.09 seconds, improving the previous record of 22.11 seconds held by Russia's Kliment Kolesnikov. Coetze won the gold medal in the 25-metre pool competition. The event is particularly significant because men's 50-metre backstroke is scheduled to make its Olympic debut at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, although Olympic swimming events use 50-metre pools. On 6 October 2026, World Archery confirmed that India had secured three archery quota places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics through the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan. Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Rajesh Jadhav earned the historic compound mixed-team quota after defeating South Korea's Park Jungyoon and Choi Yonghee in a 20–19 shoot-off. Kumukum Anil Mohod secured another quota in women's recurve archery. India's men's and women's hockey teams also qualified for LA28 by winning gold at the Asian Games, with the men's team defeating Malaysia 5–1 in the final. On 9 October 2026, Rugby India and New Zealand Rugby announced an Under-20 rugby sevens series to be held from 22 to 28 October 2026 at the Rajgir Sports Complex in Bihar. New Zealand's Māori U20 teams, Tama Toa (men) and Hine Toa (women), will visit India for four competitive matches involving Indian U20 players. The visiting contingent comprises 24 players and six management personnel. The series forms part of celebrations marking 100 years of sporting cooperation between India and New Zealand and aims to promote international competition, cultural exchange and youth rugby development. On 10 October 2026, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced that the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games 2026 would take place on 12 October at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya is scheduled to inaugurate the event, organised jointly with the Gujarat Government under India's BRICS Chairship. The non-competitive event will showcase traditional sports, including India's Mallakhamb, Yogasana and Kalaripayattu, alongside indigenous sporting practices from other participating countries. Its objectives include cultural exchange, heritage preservation and international sports cooperation. Science & Technology: On 8 October 2026, NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission successfully returned to Earth after 237 days in orbit. The Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles, California. The four returning astronauts were Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway of NASA, Sophie Adenot of the European Space Agency (ESA), and Andrey Fedyaev of Roscosmos. Launched on 13 February 2026, the mission involved scientific experiments and maintenance aboard the International Space Station (ISS). title: Algorithmic age: The death of judgement

title: Gujarat plans unified CCTV dashboard, to integrate student-built tech into policing: Dy CM
excerpt: Surat, Oct 10 (IANS) The Gujarat government aims to connect all CCTV cameras across the state to a single dashboard and integrate technology developed by young innovators into police procedures, including FIR registration and cybercrime resolution, Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said on Saturday. Addressing the grand finale of the E-Rakshak Hackathon at Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology (SVNIT) in Surat, Sanghavi said the state government wanted to encourage software-based solutions that could improve policing and reduce dependence on frequently changing hardware. He reviewed cybersecurity prototypes developed by 31 teams representing colleges affiliated with more than 13 universities across six states. The grand finale brought together 150 students, selected from 458 registrations received from across the country. Custom Ad: Multiplex "Changes in hardware and camera models introduced by major companies could increase government expenditure, making sustainable software solutions an important priority," he said. He encouraged students to use their technical expertise to address practical challenges faced by citizens and the police. He also highlighted the potential of artificial intelligence integrated with CCTV cameras to improve traffic management. "Even a 15-second reduction in waiting time at traffic signals could save millions of people valuable time and fuel," he added. The Deputy Chief Minister urged young people to look beyond social media discussions and familiarise themselves with government schemes designed to support entrepreneurship. He referred to Gujarat's industrial and startup policies, initiatives for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and schemes in the science and technology sector. "Eligible entrepreneurs could receive assistance for office rent, marketing, operational expenses, salaries and cloud subscriptions, besides support available through the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme," he noted. He also highlighted provisions for women entrepreneurs. Assuring the participants of government support, Sanghavi said the state is prepared to act as a risk partner for startups and share the risks involved in turning innovative ideas into practical solutions. Sanghavi also commended the Surat Cyber Crime Team for dismantling cybercrime rackets operating at national and international levels. "The government wanted to work with young innovators to develop technology that could help prevent crime and improve the efficiency of police operations," he said. Surat Police Commissioner Wabang Jamir said the hackathon is jointly organised by Surat City Police and SVNIT's NEXUS unit to encourage college students to develop technological solutions for cybersecurity, digital safety and cybercrime prevention. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Cyber Crime) Bishakha Jain said organisers had identified nine to 10 problem statements through surveys conducted at police stations. "These focused on everyday difficulties faced by citizens and operational challenges encountered by police personnel," she said. A total of 458 students from colleges across the country registered for the hackathon, with 150 students representing 31 teams reaching the grand finale in Surat. The initiative aims to promote more efficient policing through technology and encourage students to develop solutions that can be applied to real-world challenges. The event brought together student innovators, police officials and academic institutions to explore how emerging technologies could strengthen cybersecurity and improve public services. -- IANS mys/brt

It estimates that 4.5% of existing jobs in low- and middle-income countries face automation risks, compared with 14.2% in high-income countries. It also identifies opportunities for productivity improvements in developing economies. The report recommends an Adopt, Adapt and Advance framework, emphasising digital infrastructure, local-language data, electricity, skills and institutional capacity. Sports: On 9 October 2026, Delhi golfer Keya Kumar Badugu won the women's title at the IGU Bio-Gen Rotary Southern India Golf Championship for Ladies and Junior Girls. The competition was held at the Karnataka Golf Association course in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Badugu defeated Kolkata's Anaahat Bindra in a playoff after both golfers completed the 54-hole competition with identical scores of one-under-par 215. Badugu recorded rounds of 73, 71 and 71, while Bindra scored 70, 72 and 73. Priya Kumari finished third with an aggregate score of 220. On 9 October 2026, South African swimmer Pieter Coetze established a new world record in the men's 50-metre backstroke (short-course) event at the World Aquatics Swimming World Cup in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. He completed the event in 22.09 seconds, improving the previous record of 22.11 seconds held by Russia's Kliment Kolesnikov. Coetze won the gold medal in the 25-metre pool competition. The event is particularly significant because men's 50-metre backstroke is scheduled to make its Olympic debut at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, although Olympic swimming events use 50-metre pools. On 6 October 2026, World Archery confirmed that India had secured three archery quota places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics through the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan. Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Rajesh Jadhav earned the historic compound mixed-team quota after defeating South Korea's Park Jungyoon and Choi Yonghee in a 20–19 shoot-off. Kumukum Anil Mohod secured another quota in women's recurve archery. India's men's and women's hockey teams also qualified for LA28 by winning gold at the Asian Games, with the men's team defeating Malaysia 5–1 in the final. On 9 October 2026, Rugby India and New Zealand Rugby announced an Under-20 rugby sevens series to be held from 22 to 28 October 2026 at the Rajgir Sports Complex in Bihar. New Zealand's Māori U20 teams, Tama Toa (men) and Hine Toa (women), will visit India for four competitive matches involving Indian U20 players. The visiting contingent comprises 24 players and six management personnel. The series forms part of celebrations marking 100 years of sporting cooperation between India and New Zealand and aims to promote international competition, cultural exchange and youth rugby development. On 10 October 2026, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced that the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games 2026 would take place on 12 October at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya is scheduled to inaugurate the event, organised jointly with the Gujarat Government under India's BRICS Chairship. The non-competitive event will showcase traditional sports, including India's Mallakhamb, Yogasana and Kalaripayattu, alongside indigenous sporting practices from other participating countries. Its objectives include cultural exchange, heritage preservation and international sports cooperation. Science & Technology: On 8 October 2026, NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission successfully returned to Earth after 237 days in orbit. The Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles, California. The four returning astronauts were Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway of NASA, Sophie Adenot of the European Space Agency (ESA), and Andrey Fedyaev of Roscosmos. Launched on 13 February 2026, the mission involved scientific experiments and maintenance aboard the International Space Station (ISS). The crew travelled more than 100 million miles during the mission. On 8 October 2026, the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) released findings from its Living Planet Report 2026, titled The Science of Hope. The report revealed a 73% average decline in monitored vertebrate wildlife population sizes between 1970 and 2022. Prepared using the Living Planet Index developed by the Zoological Society of London, the analysis covered 35,803 population trends across 5,790 species. Freshwater populations experienced the largest average decline at 85%, followed by terrestrial populations at 69% and marine populations at 59%. The findings highlight the importance of biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration. On 9 October 2026, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) granted a Type Certificate to Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited (KICL) for its KOAIR-10L agricultural drone. The certificate, numbered T09260000127/00, was issued under the Drone Rules, 2021. The KOAIR-10L is a medium-class hexacopter equipped with a 10-litre tank for spraying agrochemicals. Type certification verifies that a drone model meets applicable design and technical requirements. The development supports the adoption of precision agriculture, improved spraying efficiency and domestic manufacturing of unmanned aircraft systems in India. Defence: On 9 October 2026, the Indian Coast Guard commissioned the indigenously built Fast Patrol Vessel ICGS Ajit at Goa Shipyard Limited in Goa. The vessel is intended to strengthen coastal surveillance and maritime-security operations from Okha in Gujarat. Its roles include anti-smuggling patrols, search-and-rescue missions, maritime law enforcement and environmental protection. Equipped with modern navigation and communication systems, the vessel is part of India's efforts to expand indigenous shipbuilding capacity. Its induction reinforces the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative while strengthening the Indian Coast Guard's ability to protect the country's western coastline. On 9 October 2026, the Ministry of Defence announced that INS Mangrol would be commissioned into the Indian Navy on 12 October 2026 at the Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The vessel is the third Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) built by Cochin Shipyard Limited, Kochi. The commissioning ceremony will be presided over by Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. Named after the coastal town of Mangrol in Gujarat, the indigenous vessel is designed to detect and counter underwater threats in shallow coastal waters. On 9 October 2026, the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar awarded its first Master of Technology degrees in Defence Technology to 59 Indian Army officers. The officers completed the programme through the Armoured Corps Centre and School (ACC&S), Ahilyanagar, Maharashtra. IIT Ropar Director Professor Rajeev Ahuja presented the degrees at the institution. The specialised programme combines academic research with military technology training, covering advanced armoured-vehicle systems, applied engineering and defence innovation. It aims to develop technically skilled military officers and support the modernisation and indigenisation of India's armed forces. Awards & Honours: On 9 October 2026, the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced that South African jurist Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay had won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The award recognises her efforts to promote peace and international law, particularly through work supporting accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. Born in Durban, South Africa, to a family of Indian Tamil origin, Pillay previously served as the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and as a judge at international criminal tribunals. The Nobel Committee highlighted her contribution to strengthening international justice and protecting human rights. On 9 October 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh presented 15 SIDM Champion Awards 2026 at the eighth Annual Session of the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers in New Delhi. The awards recognised organisations contributing to indigenous defence technology, product innovation, design, manufacturing, import substitution and defence exports. The event's theme was Sovereign Capabilities, Contested Frontiers: Accelerating India's Strategic Autonomy in an Era of Disruption. Rajnath Singh highlighted India's record defence exports of ₹38,424 crore in FY 2025–26 and encouraged greater private-sector participation and investment in research and development. On 8 October 2026, United States President Donald Trump presented National Medals of Science and National Medals of Technology and Innovation to six technology leaders at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit. The National Medal of Science recipients were Elon Musk, Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang and Lisa Su. The National Medal of Technology and Innovation recipients were Michael Dell and Satya Nadella. The awards recognised contributions to space technology, information retrieval, semiconductors, computing and digital infrastructure. The ceremony highlighted the importance of scientific research and technological innovation in maintaining industrial competitiveness. Committees: On 10 October 2026, the Supreme Court of India constituted a Standing Committee on Judicial Well-being under the chairmanship of Justice K.V. Viswanathan. The committee was established by Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on World Mental Health Day. Its purpose is to examine occupational stress, excessive workloads, mental-health challenges and working conditions affecting judicial officers. Other members include psychiatrist Dr. Savita Malhotra, psychologist Rajat Mitra, Advocate-on-Record Mrinal Kanwar and Supreme Court Registrar Aarti Singh. The initiative aims to strengthen institutional support and improve the effectiveness and sustainability of the justice delivery system. Summits & Conferences On 9 October 2026, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced that CyberTech Asia 2027 would be held in Mumbai in March 2027. The announcement followed discussions with CyberTech Global founder Amir Rapaport and Israeli Consul General Yaniv Revach at the Chief Minister's official residence in Mumbai. The conference is expected to bring together cybersecurity experts, technology companies, policymakers and industry representatives. Discussions will focus on emerging digital threats, technological innovation and cybersecurity cooperation. The announcement also highlighted Maharashtra's MahaCyber initiative, which aims to strengthen responses to cybercrime and online fraud. On 9 October 2026, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs organised the Second Regional Review Conference on implementation of the Forest Rights Act, 2006, in Kolkata, West Bengal. Representatives from eight states, West Bengal, Assam, Tripura, Jharkhand, Odisha, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, reviewed progress in recognising individual and community forest rights. The discussions addressed pending claims, incorporation of forest-rights titles into government records, Community Forest Resource Rights and habitat rights of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs). Andhra Pradesh officials also shared good practices in digitisation and livelihood support for forest-rights holders. Appointments: On 1 October 2026, the Reserve Bank of India approved the appointment of Anup Bagchi as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of HDFC Bank for three years, effective 27 October 2026. He will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose tenure ends on 26 October. Bagchi previously served as MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. HDFC Bank has proposed an annual remuneration package of up to ₹35.90 crore, including performance-linked compensation and stock options, potentially making him India's highest-paid bank CEO. His appointment and remuneration remain subject to the applicable shareholder approvals. On 9 October 2026, US President Donald Trump reportedly selected conservative political commentator Katie Zacharia as the next White House Press Secretary. She was chosen to succeed Karoline Leavitt, who left the position in August 2026. Zacharia previously worked as a spokesperson for the US Department of Homeland Security and served as a senior communications adviser to Trump Media & Technology Group, the parent company of Truth Social. She also appeared as a political commentator on Fox News and Newsmax. Important Days: World Mental Health Day was observed on 10 October 2026 with the World Health Organization's theme, Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change. The day promotes mental-health awareness, accessible treatment, reduced stigma and participation by people with lived experiences in healthcare decisions. In India, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare highlighted the Tele-MANAS helpline 14416, which provides free, confidential, 24-hour mental-health support. Launched on 10 October 2022, Tele-MANAS has received over 47.75 lakh calls, with 53 operational centres across 36 states and Union Territories. Obituaries: On 30 September 2026, American computer scientist Margaret Hamilton, a pioneer of software engineering, passed away in Cambridge, Massachusetts, at the age of 90. Her death was announced by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) on 7 October. Hamilton is best known for leading the team that developed onboard flight software for NASA's Apollo missions, including the historic Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969. Her work on fault-tolerant software helped ensure mission safety. She later founded software companies and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016 for her contributions to computing and space exploration. On 8 October 2026, veteran Indian freedom fighter and socialist activist P. Vasu, popularly known as 'Socio Vasu', passed away at his residence in Cheruvannur, Kozhikode, Kerala, aged 103. Born in January 1923, Vasu became involved in the independence movement after attending a public meeting addressed by Mahatma Gandhi in 1934. He participated in the Quit India Movement of 1942 and organised anti-colonial protests, for which he was imprisoned by British authorities.
